name: chart_selector.py
summary: AI-driven service that selects optimal chart types and visualization configurations based on data characteristics and query intent.
purpose: Automates the decision-making process for data visualization by bridging raw data semantics and user intent, eliminating manual chart selection and ensuring consistent, meaningful visual representations across the analytics platform.
responsibilities: Analyze dataset schema, cardinality, and statistical distributions
Interpret natural language query intent from ai_query_service
Map data characteristics to appropriate chart types and encodings
Generate chart specifications including axes, dimensions, and measures
Validate chart feasibility against data constraints
inputs: Business domain context or visualization constraints
outputs: Structured chart configuration (Vega-Lite, ECharts, or internal spec)
Fallback alternatives when data is ambiguous
architecture_notes: Operates as a domain service within the AI backend layer, likely implementing a Strategy or Rules-Engine pattern to decouple chart selection logic from rendering. It consumes intent from ai_query_service and acts as a decision authority before the presentation layer. Should remain stateless and rely on pure functions or lightweight ML inference for scalability.
improvements: Introduce a pluggable chart-strategy registry to support custom visualization types
Add confidence scores and explanation traces for each recommendation
Implement caching for recurring schema-to-chart mappings to reduce latency
Add adversarial testing for edge cases (empty datasets, high cardinality, single-column data)
Expose a feedback endpoint to capture user corrections and enable model refinement
